headline: A cheaper robotaxi opens to everyone

sources.title: Waymo's cheaper, next-gen robotaxi is now open to all riders in these three cities (TechCrunch)
Waymo's New Robotaxi Minivans Are Now Taking Paying Passengers (InsideEVs)
Waymo begins public rides in Ojai as it shifts to lower-cost robotaxis (video, CNBC)

chunks.text: In three big US cities, a taxi with no driver just became normal. Waymo's newest robotaxi, a [[roomy]] electric [[minivan]] called the Ojai, is now open to everyone in Los Angeles, Phoenix, and San Francisco. The vans have been {{showing up}} in [[traffic]] next to regular cars all summer, but riders could not choose one until now. Today, anyone with the app can {{hop in}} when their car arrives, with no one [[behind the wheel]].

verbs.why: Guests, buses, and taxis show up, or they do not. Here the car shows up by itself, with nobody behind the wheel.
Hop in the car, hop in a taxi: quick, casual entering. Riders just hop in when their van arrives.

chunks.text: The Ojai is built to cost less. The base van comes from China, but it arrives without its Chinese internet [[software]]: Waymo {{takes out}} that system and {{puts in}} its own [[self-driving]] brain at a [[factory]] in Arizona. Each van is cheaper to build and run than the Jaguar cars the company used before. There is one problem: [[import taxes]] {{push up}} the price of every van that crosses the ocean.

verbs.wrong: To test something one more time
verbs.why: You take out the trash, a splinter, or an old part. Waymo takes out the Chinese software before installing its own.
You put in batteries, a new kitchen, or long hours. Waymo puts in its own self-driving brain at a factory in Arizona.
Taxes, demand, and shortages push up prices. Import taxes push up the cost of every van that crosses the ocean.

chunks.text: Riding in one feels simple. [[Passengers]] sit down, {{buckle up}}, and press a button. The van joins traffic [[on its own]]. A talking [[assistant]] answers questions during the ride. For now, the app [[decides]] which car you get, so riders {{end up}} with either the new van or an older Jaguar. Soon, riders will be able to {{pick out}} the [[model]] they want right in the app.

verbs.why: Buckle up in a car, a plane, or a rollercoaster. Passengers sit, buckle up, press a button, and the van drives.

verbs.wrong: To trade one thing for another
verbs.why: You end up with the last slice, the middle seat, or whatever remains. For now riders end up with whichever car the app sends.
You pick out clothes, paint colors, or a puppy. Soon riders can pick out the exact model they want in the app.

chunks.text: Waymo is [[moving fast]]. About 300 of the new vans are [[on the road]] today, and one [[analyst]] expects the [[fleet]] to reach 5,000 [[by the end of the year]]. The company also plans to {{roll out}} the service in Denver, Las Vegas, and San Diego later this year. [[Driverless]] rides are [[no longer]] a science [[experiment]]. The question now is price: will cheaper vans mean cheaper rides, and will lower prices {{win over}} people who still {{hold back}}?

verbs.why: Companies roll out services city by city. This one rolls out next to Denver, Las Vegas, and San Diego.

verbs.wrong: To beat someone in a race
verbs.why: Politicians win over voters, and brands win over doubters. Cheaper rides might win over people who still fear a driverless car.

verbs.correct: To wait because of fear or doubt
verbs.why: You hold back when the water looks cold or the ride looks scary. Some riders still hold back from the empty driver's seat.

mainIdea.s: Waymo has opened its cheaper new robotaxi, a driverless minivan, to all riders in three US cities. The company plans thousands more vans and new cities this year.
mainIdea.why: The Ojai is now open to everyone in Los Angeles, Phoenix, and San Francisco, with about 300 vans today and big growth plans.

mainIdea.s: Waymo now lets every rider choose exactly which robotaxi model picks them up. The new choice arrived this month in Los Angeles, Phoenix, and San Francisco.
mainIdea.why: Close, but riders cannot pick the model yet. The app decides which car arrives, and choosing will only come later.

mainIdea.s: A new law lets teenagers ride city buses for free in three big US cities. Officials hope the plan will cut traffic and help students reach school on time.
mainIdea.why: The article is about Waymo opening its driverless minivan to all riders, not about free buses for teenagers.
